name: code-embed-vscode
description: Local hybrid (semantic + lexical) code search for VS Code and AI agents

codeEmbed.embedding.provider.description: Embedding provider: "local" (built-in model) or the name of a provider from codeEmbed.providers.

codeEmbed.providers.markdownDescription: OpenAI-compatible embedding providers: name → configuration. Easier to manage on the [settings page](command:codeEmbed.openSettings). Do not put API keys here; use `api_key_env` or the settings page, which keeps keys in VS Code secret storage.

base_url.description: Base URL of the API, e.g. http://localhost:11434/v1

api_key_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the API key.

codeEmbed.model.id.description: Local embedding model from the built-in catalog (see "Code Embed: Select Model").

codeEmbed.model.offlineArchive.description: Path to an offline model archive to install from instead of downloading.

enumDescriptions: Inside the project (.code-embed/), or in the user cache when the project is on a risky file system (network drive, cloud sync).
Always in the user cache directory.

codeEmbed.index.maxFileKb.description: Files larger than this (in KB) are not indexed.

codeEmbed.index.threads.description: Hard limit on threads used by local models on this machine, shared by all VS Code windows, the CLI and MCP (0 = automatic: half of the cores, at most 4). If windows or the CLI set different values, the smallest one applies

codeEmbed.index.pauseOnBattery.description: Pause the vector phase of indexing while running on battery.

codeEmbed.index.exclude.description: Glob patterns of files to skip, in addition to .gitignore, files.exclude and search.exclude.

languageModelTools.name: code-embed_search
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search the workspace code by meaning and keywords.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Hybrid (semantic + lexical) search over a local index of the current workspace's code. Use it instead of grep/ripgrep when searching by meaning: questions like "where is X handled" or "how does Y work", finding the implementation of a concept or behavior when you do not know the exact identifiers, natural-language queries in any language (including Russian), or when grep returns nothing or too much noise. Do NOT use it for an exact identifier, string literal, error message or file name: use grep/ripgrep or file search for exact matches. Do NOT use it to list the callers or usages of a symbol: use references. To see the surroundings of a found chunk (callees, callers, tests, related code), use context. Returns ranked code chunks (path, line range, symbol, snippet); read the referenced lines for full context. Narrow the search with include/exclude globs and lang when you know where to look.

query.description: What to look for, in natural language or keywords, e.g. "where is the payment refund processed" or "retry with exponential backoff". Any language, including Russian.

mode.description: hybrid (default) combines meaning and keywords; semantic matches by meaning only; lexical matches keywords and identifiers only.

top.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-50).

include.description: Glob patterns relative to the workspace root; only matching files are searched, e.g. ["src/**"].

exclude.description: Glob patterns relative to the workspace root to skip, e.g. ["**/*.test.ts"].

lang.description: Restrict results to one language id, e.g. typescript, python, go, rust, markdown.

languageModelTools.name: code-embed_find_similar
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find code similar to a fragment or a range of lines.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find code in the current workspace that is semantically similar to a given fragment: duplicates, near-copies, alternative implementations of the same logic, other places that follow the same pattern. Pass either a location (path relative to the workspace root, start_line and end_line, 1-based inclusive) or a code snippet (code, optional lang). Use it before a refactoring or a bug fix to find other places that need the same change. Do NOT use it to find callers or usages of a symbol: use references. To see the surroundings of a fragment (callees, callers, tests), use context. Returns ranked code chunks (path, line range, symbol, snippet).

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root (use together with start_line and end_line).

start_line.description: First line of the fragment, 1-based, inclusive.

end_line.description: Last line of the fragment, 1-based, inclusive.

code.description: Code fragment to compare against (use instead of path/start_line/end_line).

lang.description: Language id of `code`, e.g. typescript, python. Only with `code`.

top.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-50).

languageModelTools.name: code-embed_outline
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the symbols of a file with signatures and line ranges.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the symbols of one file from the local index: classes, functions, methods and other declarations with kind, signature, parent symbol and line range, ordered by position. Use it to get the structure of a file without reading it whole, then read only the lines you need. Takes a path relative to the workspace root. Returns an empty list if the file is not indexed.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root.

languageModelTools.name: code-embed_references
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find the definitions and usages of a symbol by name.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find where a symbol is defined and where it is used (calls, type references, imports) across the current workspace. Use it to answer "who calls X" or "where is X used" instead of grep. The lookup is name-based, from the local index: it matches identifiers by name and does not resolve scopes or types, so it is NOT a replacement for LSP (language server) find-references. Every item has a confidence, high or low; treat low-confidence items as candidates and verify them in the code. Optional path restricts definitions to one file. Returns definitions first, then usages (path, line range, line, kind, confidence, source line).

symbol.description: Symbol name to look up, e.g. "processRefund" or "PaymentService".

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root; restricts definitions to this file.

languageModelTools.name: code-embed_context
languageModelTools.userDescription: Collect the code around a location or query: callees, callers, tests, similar code.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Collect the working context of a piece of code in one call: the target chunk plus its callees, callers, tests, similar code and recent commits of the file, ordered by priority and cut to a token budget. Pass either a location (path relative to the workspace root and line, 1-based) or a query (natural language or symbol name). Use it before changing code to see what it depends on and what depends on it. Optional budget_tokens sets the size limit of the answer; the default is 4000 tokens. Levels that did not fit in the budget are reported as omitted.

path.description: File path relative to the workspace root (use together with line).

query.description: Natural-language description or symbol name of the target (use instead of path/line).

budget_tokens.description: Token budget for the whole answer (default 4000).
